Hi Jane — thanks for the clear breakdown. Short answers up front: Dedicated pools are included in our SOC 2 Type II; customer-managed Private/VPC/on-prem deployments are generally out-of-scope for the standard report and are treated as customer-controlled environments.

Details and next steps:
- Coverage: Our public/hosted API and Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools we operate for a customer) are covered by the Type II report. That includes controls around change management, access, monitoring, and incident response for those hosted/dedicated environments.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: Because those environments are customer-managed (network, OS, KMS, etc.), they are typically excluded from the standard SOC 2 unless we have a specific managed-support engagement where Redwood operates significant controls in the customer's environment.
- Bridge letter: We can produce a bridge letter that: (a) confirms the audit period (example: 2026-06-01 to 2026-11-30), (b) lists in-scope services (Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated), and (c) explicitly states Private/VPC/on-prem are excluded from the scope of the report. We'll provide a draft for your legal/security teams to review.

ETA and artifacts: I will escalate to our compliance team to pull the signed SOC 2 Type II for the requested window (if available) and draft the bridge letter. Target timeline: provide the SOC 2 PDF and a draft bridge letter within 5 business days (by 2026-12-06); if any variance occurs I'll flag immediately.

If helpful, can we set a 30-minute call early next week to run through the wording Acme needs?
